explanations: A partition only preserves the order in which sends succeed. When a send fails transiently, flush() pushes that event onto the end of the buffer and moves on to the next events in the batch. Later updates for the same order (picked_up, delivered) are sent first, and the failed one (accepted) follows on a later flush. The tracking projection trusts partition order, so it ends on the stale status and pushes the notifications out of order. The fix stops the flush at the first failed send and puts that event, together with everything behind it, back at the front of the buffer in its original order. The next flush then resumes exactly where it left off. A per-order variant (hold back only later events for the same orderId) also works.
